newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek ministers to visit Albania bearing aid.
newsitem.headline: Greek ministers to visit Albania bearing aid.

text.p: Greece, keen to see neighbouring Albania back on its feet, will send a group of ministers to the troubled Balkan state on Tuesday to help rebuild its shattered economy, police and armed forces.

The delegation, led by Foreign Minister Theodoros Pangalos, will include Public Order Minister George Romeos and five deputy ministers. It will be the first foreign visit to Tirana since a new Albanian government was elected in June.
"Half the Greek cabinet will be in Tirana," a senior Greek diplomat told Reuters. "Greece wants restored stability and the fastest possible progress in Albania."
More than 1,500 people have been killed in Albania since March, when bogus pyramid investment schemes collapsed and left tens of thousands destitute.

Albanians looted an estimated one million weapons from army and police depots, triggering months of anarchy which led to the fall of the Democratic Party government and the resignation of president Sali Berisha.

Greece, which has seen a heavy inflow of illegal Albanian immigrants fleeing the violence and poverty in their country, is eager for stability to be restored to its northern border, the diplomat said.

It will offer Albania's new Prime Minister Fatos Nano, head of the Socialist-led coalition government elected in June, a $20 million loan and help to re-organise the chaotic police and army. Greece will also offer temporary work to Albanian immigrants.
"We will offer no arms, only organisational help," the diplomat said. "We will also finalise the temporary employment issue and discuss the terms of the new loan."
Greece's defence, national economy, public works and labour ministries will also send deputy ministers to discuss these issues with their Albanian counterparts.
The Greek public order ministry, which has borne the brunt of a new crime wave imported from Albania since March, will ask Tirana for help in improving the patrolling of borders.
"We will demand to be given, at long last, a list of Albanian criminals who have escaped from prison in recent months," Romeos told an Athens daily.

The minister said crime committed by Albanian nationals in Greece had risen considerably since March. Southern Albania remains at the mercy of armed bands, and roads linking towns to the capital are often violent.
The world community has been eager to help Albania stabilise. A meeting of international donors is due in Brussels in October to examine ways to provide aid in the form of approved projects.
